newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen stuck in Tokyo, ignores EPA, BOJ.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen stuck in Tokyo, ignores EPA, BOJ.

text.p: The benchmark March three-month Euroyen contract on TIFFE was stuck in a narrow trading range on Friday, shrugging off comments from an Economic Planning Agency (EPA) official and Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Yasuo Matsushita, traders said.
The key three-month certificate of deposit was at 0.51-52 percent against Wednesday's 0.52. The overnight call rate was most actively traded at 0.45 percent, unchanged from Wednesday.
The market is waiting for the outcome of Japan's general elections on October 20.

Shoji Kitta, managing director of Tokyo Tanshi Co Ltd, the largest money broker in Japan, said; "The economy would recover at a faster pace and rates would go up, if the new coalition government were able to put in place measures to revitalise transactions in land and raise the liquidity of it."

He said it was also vital to implement a new type of supplementary budget which does not put an emphasis on public works spending as the effectiveness of that spending has already been proven to be limited.
These policy priorities could be ignored if the Socialist Party or the Sakigake Party became a member of the coalition.
They have been opposed to any changes in the current land tax system, saying they would only help the wealthy.
The market greeted with a yawn remarks by an EPA official after its regular monthly economic outlook, as well as BOJ Governor Matsushita's speech, traders said.
"No one feels that the economy is rapidly recovering, but nor are there bad or worsening factors to worry about," the official said.
Matsushita told a meeting of business executives that the central bank's monetary policy would continue to be aimed at ensuring a firm basis for economic recovery.
Matsushita also said that the low interest rates have helped the economy recover.
But capital spending and private consumption must strengthen further for Japan's economy to achieve an autonomous recovery, he added.
